items.stem: What does the photovoltaic effect describe?

options.text: Generation of an electric current when light frees charge carriers in a semiconductor
options.rationale: That is the photovoltaic effect at the heart of a PV cell.

options.text: Storage of electricity in a chemical battery
options.rationale: That is electrochemical storage, not the PV effect.

options.text: Conversion of sunlight directly into heat for hot water
options.rationale: That describes solar thermal, not photovoltaics.

options.text: Rotation of a turbine by wind pressure
options.rationale: That is wind energy, unrelated to the PV effect.

items.explanation: That is the photovoltaic effect at the heart of a PV cell.

items.stem: Which TWO factors reduce the real-world energy yield of a PV array below its nameplate rating? (Select TWO.)

options.text: High cell temperature on hot sunny days
options.rationale: PV output falls as cell temperature rises above the rated condition.

options.text: Partial shading of modules in a string
options.rationale: Shading on one module can disproportionately cut string output.

options.text: Using a module with a higher efficiency rating
options.rationale: Higher efficiency raises, not reduces, yield.

options.text: Orienting the array toward the equator at optimal tilt

items.explanation: PV output falls as cell temperature rises above the rated condition.

items.stem: A grid-tied PV system without battery backup stops producing usable power during a grid outage. Why?

options.text: The inverter must disconnect for safety (anti-islanding) when the grid is down
options.rationale: Anti-islanding protection prevents back-feeding a dead grid, so a basic grid-tied inverter shuts off.

options.text: The panels physically stop absorbing light during outages
options.rationale: Panels still receive light; the inverter disconnects.

options.text: Grid outages drain the panels of stored charge
options.rationale: Panels store no charge; there is no battery in this system.
No polarity reversal occurs; the cause is anti-islanding.

items.explanation: Anti-islanding protection prevents back-feeding a dead grid, so a basic grid-tied inverter shuts off.
